learningObjective: Reason about how acceptance rate determines speedup in speculative decoding and where speedup is bounded.

canonicalClaims.claim: Under Bernoulli-independent acceptance with per-token probability p, expected accepted prefix length is (1 - p^{k+1})/(1 - p); speedup is bounded by (k+1) but the actual value depends on both p and the draft/target cost ratio.
conditions: Draft and target costs are known.
Per-token acceptance is approximated as Bernoulli independent.
nonImplications: Does not imply larger k is always better; variance grows and diminishing returns kick in.
Does not imply draft can run in parallel with target on the critical path.

misconceptions.claim: Speculative decoding gives fixed k× speedup.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Actual acceptance is <k on average when p<1.

misconceptions.claim: Speedup only depends on p, not on k.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Both k and p appear in the expected-prefix formula.

misconceptions.claim: Draft model runs in parallel with target model on the same GPU.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Draft is sequential per step; some pipelining is possible but does not eliminate draft cost.

implementationFacts: k is typically 3-8; larger k adds variance and diminishing returns.
Medusa and EAGLE replace an external draft model with additional heads on the target for cheaper drafting.
performanceScenarios: Speedup is largest when target is bandwidth-bound (decode) and draft is a fraction of target cost.
Speedup diminishes when p is low or when draft is not much cheaper than target.
